user_summary:
Brief 5 is finished and checked: Fire-3d now shows floods in the lower 48 states as well as wildfires. Here is what you get, in plain words.

Where to find floods
- At the top of the national map there is a small switch: Fires | Floods. Pick Floods and the map lists every flood the National Weather Service (NWS) is warning about right now, plus river gauges that read at flood stage. Each blue circle is one flood; a bigger circle groups several ('12 FLOODS'). Click one to open it.
- 'Show details' opens the list, with tabs for today's floods and for past floods of 2026 and 2025 (the bigger ones: rivers that reached moderate or major flood stage, and flash floods NWS called considerable, catastrophic or an emergency). Flood Watches (flooding possible, not yet happening) are hidden until you turn on 'Show watches'.

The three flood views
- Public: the place and dates, a round 'water circle' with the NWS status (for example FLOOD · WARNING), and seven plain facts, each with who said it and when: NWS's forecast flooded area, the river level measured at the main gauge, the NWS forecast peak (crest), the warning in effect, evacuations and the last official update.
- Command: for experts. Click any spot on the map to see which layers cover it and the nearest gauge; 'Official now' lists every NWS message word for word; a river-level chart runs along the bottom. Drag its handle to see the river level and the NWS messages at another time.
- Forensic: the flood layers draped on 3D terrain. Press 'Prepare 3D data (about 1 min)' the first time. River gauges appear as thin bars (bar height = river level at the gauge, scaled, not water depth).

What the colours and lines mean
- Pink outlines: NWS warning areas (official).
- Solid blue: water seen by satellite. Grey hatching: the satellite could not see there (clouds or no data); a thin dashed grey line is the edge of the satellite picture.
- Blue hatching: the NWS forecast flooded area for the next 5 days (NWS calls this map experimental).
- Dashed blue outline: the river's main channel.
- Diamonds are river gauges, coloured by NWS flood category: yellow = action stage (near flood stage), orange = minor flooding, red = moderate, purple = major; a grey hollow diamond = below flood stage. The category is always written next to the colour.
- The light-blue dot with a label is the point you selected.
- In the river chart: the solid light-blue line is measured (USGS), the dashed white line is the NWS forecast, the coloured horizontal lines are NWS flood levels, and the small caret marks the forecast crest.
- Dotted amber: the National Water Model, a computer model (only in Command and Forensic, and only when you switch it on).

Official versus experimental
- Official: NWS warnings and their wording, NWS river forecasts and flood categories, FEMA's flood zones and evacuation orders. They always keep their sender, their own times and a link, and are never mixed with anything else.
- Measured: river levels from USGS gauges (provisional data) and water seen by satellite.
- Experimental: NWS's forecast and category flood maps (NWS's own label) and NOAA's National Water Model (model output, never in Public).
- Fire-3d has no flood model of its own. Nothing here is advice on when to evacuate, and nothing is an all-clear: a gauge below flood stage, a missing warning or a dry-looking satellite pixel does not mean there is no flooding. Follow local officials.

What the satellite layer can and cannot see
- It shows water NASA's satellites (Landsat and Sentinel-2) measured on their last clear pass. That pass is often several days old (the age is shown, in amber after 3 days).
- It cannot see through clouds, under trees or between buildings, and it includes the river's normal water. Grey hatching marks the places it could not see.

Optional: the NASA token (adds radar images that see through clouds)
1. Make a free account at urs.earthdata.nasa.gov and choose 'Generate Token' (it lasts about 60 days; note the date).
2. Sign in once at search.earthdata.nasa.gov and download any one OPERA DSWx file, so NASA's archive approves your account.
3. Put the line EARTHDATA_TOKEN=<your token> in the .env file in the Fire-3d folder (the same file as the FIRMS key), never in chat or git. Restart Fire-3d.
Without it everything works; the satellite line says 'No radar images: NASA login not set up'. The token path has only been tested with a fake token, so tell me if the radar images do not appear.

What is left for later
- One chart per gauge side by side in Forensic's Analysis tab (today: a 'Chart' button per gauge).
- Flood names in the search suggestions, a phone-specific flood list, a closer look at mid-size (1024 px) screens.
- Your decision: at Copperhill, Tennessee, one real event shows twice (as the Toccoa / Ocoee River flood and as the Ducktown flash flood). Joining them would show river facts instead of the flash-flood facts. Tell me which you prefer.
- Try it yourself: switch to Floods, open a flood, press 'MORE IN COMMAND', drag the chart's handle, and turn on Reduce motion in macOS (the water circle should stand still).
